$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the type system. Read by the TypeScript editor AND the Rust runtime. Neither reimplements these rules — see docs/adr/0003. A conformance test asserts both readers agree on every pair.

json.label: JSON
json.doc: Arbitrary structured data. The escape hatch — conversions to and from it are always explicit.

file.label: File
file.doc: An opaque handle to a file owned by the runtime. Never a path.

dir.label: Folder
dir.doc: An opaque handle to a directory owned by the runtime.

bytes.label: Bytes
bytes.doc: Raw binary content. Deliberately NOT a subtype of file: bytes are a file's contents, not a kind of file. Modelling it as a subtype would let image -> file -> bytes look like a narrowing and break the sibling rule.

image.label: Image
image.doc: A file the runtime has verified to be a decodable image.

video.label: Video
video.doc: A file the runtime has verified to be a container with a video stream.

audio.label: Audio
audio.doc: A file the runtime has verified to be decodable audio.

$coercionKinds.direct: Same type, or a widening to a supertype. No conversion happens. Silent.
$coercionKinds.implicit: A total conversion that cannot fail for any input. Applied by the runtime, marked on the edge. Silent but visible.
$coercionKinds.explicit: Legal but MAY FAIL, or loses information. The editor materialises a Convert node the user can see and inspect. Never silent — a conversion that can fail must have a place in the graph where its failure is reported.

coercions.note: Exact for |n| < 2^53; beyond that the runtime reports a precision error rather than rounding silently.
Zero is false. Explicit because the intent is rarely obvious when reading the graph.
Loses the fractional part; the Convert node exposes the rounding mode.
Accepts only an explicit allowlist of literals.
Explicit so that a graph never turns structured data into text by accident.
Performs a read; may fail on permission or size limits.
Materialises the bytes into a run-scoped temporary file; may fail on disk space.
Narrowing. Fails if the file is not a decodable image.
Narrowing. Fails if the file has no video stream.
Narrowing. Fails if the file has no audio stream.

$genericRules.list: list<A> -> list<B> is legal when A -> B is legal; the resulting kind is the weakest of the element kind and 'direct'. An explicit element conversion makes the whole list conversion explicit.
$genericRules.option: T -> option<T> is direct (a value is always a present option). option<T> -> T is explicit, because the absent case has to be handled somewhere the user can see it.
